idea: Fault detection and tolerance chain: detect (residual vs model, isolation-forest anomaly score over a threshold, mean/std criteria on a sensor), isolate and identify the fault, reconfigure the controller, and fall back to redundancy/backup when the primary fails. For ACMS: wrap each LLM agent (TSP, DEVL) with a monitor that flags timeouts, malformed or out-of-range answers and long streaks of one answer, then switches to a deterministic backup rule (e.g. grant bus priority when lateness > X s and cross queue < Y) and logs the switch.
does: Per-agent health monitor plus rule-based backup policy, reported in the run results (how many decisions came from the backup and why).
inputs: agent responses, latency, validity checks, backup rule parameters
outputs: decision source flag per request, failure counts
existing: partial: extensions are switched off when they raise (no graceful backup policy)
cite: Ch 4 s4.5-4.6 (fault detection, isolation, reconfiguration, redundancy)
notes: The chapter's MATLAB examples are trivial (threshold on averaged sensors); the structure detect/isolate/reconfigure/backup is the useful part. A deterministic backup also acts as the no-LLM baseline for run_experiment.

idea: Calibrate a cheap reduced-order model against a high-fidelity one instead of costly field data: prescribe the detailed model's computed quantities in the cheap model, scale them for definitional mismatch (near-wall vs bulk temperature there), and judge by an accuracy-versus-compute table (seconds on one core vs 29 h on 112 cores).
does: Runs the microsimulation over a grid of demand levels and fits correction factors for the closed-form estimates ACMS already uses (Webster delay, roundabout/priority capacity, saturation flow) so planning-level tools match the simulator, reporting residual error per regime.
inputs: analytic model outputs, headless sim results at several demands/seeds
existing: partial: roundabout entry capacity measured on simulated drivers
notes: Analogy only: the book is about engine thermal models, but the reduced-order vs high-fidelity calibration pattern transfers.
